section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India — Deep 3
subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate?
explanation: The Delhi Sultanate's five dynasties ruled in this order: Slave/Mamluk (1206), Khalji (1290), Tughlaq (1320), Sayyid (1414), Lodi (1451) — ending with Babur's victory over Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526.

section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India — Deep 3
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Bhakti movement in medieval India primarily emphasised:

options.option_text: Personal devotion to God, often without caste distinction or elaborate ritual
Strict adherence to caste-based ritual as the only path to God
Military conquest as a religious duty
Rejection of all forms of worship

explanation: Bhakti saints (Kabir, Meera, Chaitanya, and in Andhra, Annamacharya/Tyagaraja tradition) stressed direct, personal devotion accessible to all, often challenging rigid caste and ritual hierarchies.

section: Social Studies · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India — Deep 3
subject: Social Studies
stem: Annamacharya, the prolific composer of devotional songs (sankeertanas) dedicated to Lord Venkateswara, is closely associated with which pilgrimage centre?
explanation: Annamacharya (15th century) composed over 32,000 sankeertanas in praise of Lord Venkateswara of Tirumala — regarded as a pioneer of Carnatic music tradition in the Telugu region.
